trickyParts: The pinned library has no path for a credential-less token exchange: it refuses a public client that grant (handler/rfc8693/flow_token_exchange.go:36) and refuses the 'none' method to a confidential one (client_authentication_strategy.go:242). RFC 8693 Section 2.1 makes client authentication a deployment decision, so the broker supplies the library's own ClientAuthenticationStrategy hook for one client id, one grant, and a request carrying no credential of any kind; everything else goes to the library untouched. The alternatives were a client secret in every pod -- the shared secret this issue removes -- or keying client authentication, which would lock out the continuous-integration caller, which has no enrolled key.

A pod's projected service-account token is a standing credential its kubelet refreshes, so single-use (ValidateJTI) on that subject-token type would refuse every renewal. It is off for the Kubernetes type and on for the GitHub one, whose runs mint a fresh token per request.

RFC8693CustomJWTTypeFactory asserts the composed strategy to jwt.Strategy, which the broker's code strategy was not. The handler uses that strategy only to issue a JSON Web Token, which this provider never does, so the method set is implemented as explicit refusals: no signing key is generated anywhere and nothing can quietly mint a signed token.

The library checks a subject token's issuer and its expiry and never its audience, so the broker checks the audience itself -- without it a token a pod was given for another service would be spendable at the exchange.

oauthstore wrote and read only *oauth2.DefaultSession. The exchange needs a session the RFC 8693 handlers can write their subject and actor claims on, and an introspection reads those claims back out of the row, so the store now round-trips both kinds.
deviations: The plan's decision D8 said the exchanging callers are public clients. That is not buildable against the pinned library, for the reason in trickyParts; the client is registered confidential and authenticates with no credential through the library's own strategy hook. Reported to the architect, who agreed and asked for the narrowness to be proved by test (it is: oauth/exchange_test.go, and live steps 6.5a and 6.5b) and for the reason to be in the pull request body (it is).

The plan's section 5 item 7 put the approver assertion in this slice, as a further configured issuer. The architect withdrew it in three steps and settled it as dispatch://INFRA-314: no approver-identity mechanism is built here, and the RFC 7523 assertion grant written for it was removed from the branch rather than left unused, since nothing presents a person-held assertion to the token endpoint.

The architect added to this slice, in its place, the removal of the broker's shared bearer: BROKER_UI_TOKEN is gone and every route it authenticated takes the caller's own Kubernetes service-account token. What those routes do with an approver's name is deliberately unchanged -- removing the bearer and the approver trust together would stop every agent secret being approved from the moment this deploys -- and the route table says so beside them.

The plan said a token's session claim comes from configuration. A Kubernetes service-account token names the account and the pod, never the agent's own session, so the exchange reads a session form parameter; a configured entry that fixes the name wins and refuses another, which is how the Legion daemon keeps the name it writes under today. The architect then required the name to be bound to the identity that first claimed it, which it is: first caller wins until its tokens lapse.

A dev box session's token carries no project, as a person's own cookie and personal token carry none. The architect required the absence to be explicit rather than missing, so every token carries a project scope and a later slice's check can refuse one carrying neither.
openQuestions: Nothing presents a broker token to Dispatch yet: Dispatch accepting one is Child A and Legion presenting one is Child D, so this slice's credential kind is inert in production until those land. That is the plan's own ordering (section 7) and not a gap in this work.

The deployment change this slice needs is listed in the pull request body under 'Deployment'. BROKER_API_ACCOUNTS is required and replaces BROKER_UI_TOKEN in the same deploy: a broker started with the old variable refuses it by name, so the two must move together.
discoveredComplexity: This pod cannot start a workload in the cluster (kubectl auth can-i create services and get services both answer no, and docs/kubernetes.md forbids submitting a Job on anything less than three bare yes answers), and it has no Docker and no psql. The live run was made possible by fetching a standalone Postgres build and running it in this pod; the harness talks to it with pgx. A role that needs a database for a live proof in this deployment has no sanctioned path until dispatch://INFRA-206's declarations are applied.

Five test packages fail in this pod for reasons that are the pod's and not the change's, and they pass in CI: internal/broker/helper, cmd/agent-secrets and cmd/agent-secrets-helper fail with 'SO_PEERPIDFD: protocol not available' (this kernel identifies no socket peer), and cmd/listener and cmd/natstail fail with 'rootless Docker not found'. Every other package of the module is green.
